collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Two children set up their own council to settle a squabble over a toy canoe: let the council rule, or ask an elder to sit in.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Two little ones are squabbling over a toy canoe, and (subject) and (friend) have decided to settle it properly, the way the grown-ups do. They've set up a council under a tree, with stones for seats and a stick for whoever is speaking. Several adults have stopped to watch, trying hard not to smile.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The children's council hears both sides very seriously. Then it rules: each little one gets the canoe for half the day, and whoever has it in the morning must let the other one help paint it. The little ones accept at once. The watching adults agree, privately, that it was a better ruling than some of theirs.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) invites (elder), an elder, to join "as an advisor." (elder) sits on a stone and says nothing at all, except once, very quietly: "Have you asked them what they want?" The council asks. It turns out both little ones want to sail the canoe in the puddle together. The council declares the case closed. (elder) looks very pleased.
